full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner was that '08.25 acres of land along with a house thereon appertaining to SA Khatian No. 948/1 of Mouza No. 34 Bahadur Khali District Kushtia as mentioned in schedule 'Ka' belonged to one Zamil Ahmed Ansari, 02.50 acres of land with a building thereon appertaining to SA Khatian No. 936 of the same mouza and district as mentioned in the schedule "Kha" of the plaint belonged to Abdul Latif Ansari and Md. Nazib Ansari equally, 02.97 acres of land along with building thereon appertaining to SA Khatian No. 854 of the same mouza and District as mentioned in schedule 'Ca' of the plaint belonged to Amir Hossain and the houses No. B 101 and B102 in the Kushtia Housing Estate as mentioned in the schedule 'Gha' of the plaint belonged to Najib Ansari and his wife Habiban Nessa. The aforesaid persons were non-Bengali muslims. Amir Hossain Ansari died earlier and was survived by two sons Abdul Latif Ansari and Najib Ansari. Both Abkul Latif Ansari and his son Jamil Ahmed Ansari were killed during the war of liberation on 11.12.1971. The only legal heir of Amir Ansari was then Najib Ansari. Najib Ansari also was killed along with his wife susequently during the said war on 18.12.1971 leaving behind his only daughter the plaintiff since their another daughter Rokeya Banu died earlier during her infancy. On their death, the plaintiff petitioner became the only legal heir of the persons mentioned above and became the absolute owner of the properties mentioned in the schedule 'Ka' to Gha' of the plaint of the suit. The plaintiff was a Bangladeshi citizen and had married a local Bengali. It is stated that the plaintiff who used to live in her father-in-law's house at Jessore came to know about the property being treated as abandoned properties for the first time in 1981 and hence filed the suit for declaration as stated above.
